title: Yoshi's Island DS
subtitle: More babies for the journey
summary: Yoshi's Island DS is Artoon's Nintendo DS platform game following the Yoshis as they rescue children kidnapped by Kamek. It extends the Super Nintendo adventure's hand-drawn appearance, egg throwing and flutter jumps across both handheld displays. The major addition is a group of babies with different abilities. Choosing who rides on Yoshi's back can change the route through a level. The rescue gives the familiar travelling partnership several new forms, letting a companion's particular skill become the key to reaching the next platform or hidden object.
body: Yoshi's Island DS is Artoon's Nintendo DS platform game following the Yoshis as they rescue children kidnapped by Kamek. It extends the Super Nintendo adventure's hand-drawn appearance, egg throwing and flutter jumps across both handheld displays. The major addition is a group of babies with different abilities. Choosing who rides on Yoshi's back can change the route through a level. The rescue gives the familiar travelling partnership several new forms, letting a companion's particular skill become the key to reaching the next platform or hidden object.

Baby Mario allows Yoshi to dash and reveal particular blocks, while Baby Peach's parasol helps him ride air currents. Baby Donkey Kong can grip vines and ropes, Baby Wario attracts metal objects with a magnet, and Baby Bowser breathes fire. Switching at the appropriate places turns the cast into a set of tools for exploration. A section that looks inaccessible with one passenger can make sense with another. The player needs to understand both Yoshi's shared movement and the extra possibility supplied by the baby currently being carried.

Yoshi can swallow enemies, turn them into eggs and aim those eggs at distant targets or switches. A hit separates him from his passenger, starting a countdown in which the baby must be recovered. That interruption makes protection a physical task inside the level rather than only a reduction in health. The tall playing area gives movement another scale, with the gap between screens becoming something to judge carefully. The familiar actions still anchor the adventure while its expanded cast supplies reasons to reconsider how a level can be crossed.
story_headings: Recover the child before time runs out
